questions.question: Raid chest looks: one per enemy faction. Any references or ideas for each?
questions.why: Decided: each of the seven enemy factions gets its own raid chest. If no references come, I'll design them from each race's palette (Marauder war crate, Black Legion strongbox, Burning Horde bone chest, Swarm chitin pod, Silverwood root-bound coffer, Ironbeard vault, Fallen Host reliquary).

settled.answer: Each race gets three of its own towers on top of the shared Arrow Tower, Arcane Spire and Healing Shrine, unlocking with base level like beasts. Human: Ballista (level 2), Watchtower Bell (level 3), Trebuchet (level 5); Elf: Thornwood Sentinel (level 2), Moonwell Grove (level 3), Elder Treant Spire (level 5); Dwarf: Rune Cannon (level 2), Stone Warden (level 3), Thunder Forge (level 5); Orc: War Drum Totem (level 2), Goblin Bomb Catapult (level 3), Waaagh Banner (level 5); Demon: Soul Pyre (level 2), Brimstone Chains (level 3), Hellgate (level 5); Angel: Sun Lance (level 2), Choir Bell (level 3), Seraphic Obelisk (level 5); Hive: Lurker Pit (level 2), Brood Nest (level 3), Synapse Spire (level 5). Only that race can build them. Race towers allowed: 2 at base level 2, 4 at level 3, 6 at level 4, 10 at level 5; each capstone is limited to one. Shared towers stay uncapped (mana limits them).

Warfront gets a clean, modern UI: flat semi-transparent dark panels with thin borders and one accent color per race (Hive cyan, demon ember, angel gold and so on). First pass: a combat HUD (race power and army status), a War Table screen on a hotkey (army roster with ranks and duties, returning heroes, base level, beasts), a base mana overlay (look at a well, pylon or tower to see its mana, range and links) and a redesigned Summoning Altar with unit cards. Toasts handle rank-ups, fallen heroes and mana warnings, a big banner announces siege events, and chat stays clean.

Veterancy: battle units climb 5 ranks (Recruit, Regular, Veteran, Elite, Legend) slowly, from kills and from surviving siege waves. Each rank adds about +10% health and damage through vanilla attributes, and Elite and Legend units don't rout. Rank shows on the unit: its armor upgrades a tier per rank and it wears rank insignia (one chevron per rank). Troops lose their rank when they die; fallen heroes keep it when revived.

Dwarves don't fly; they tunnel. A dwarf-only rune drill digs 3×3 tunnels fast, and dwarves can line them with rune stone that enemies (raiders, Hive tunnelers, explosions) struggle to break, so their tunnels are an underground fortress. Tunnel traps: a spike floor (hidden, reusable), a rune mine (explodes on enemies only, single use, costs a Mana Crystal) and a flame vent (fires down the tunnel, runs on base mana like a tower).

The Hive's Otherside reward is echo armor: Hive player armor made from Deeper and Darker's echo materials, stronger in the dark and underground, with quieter footsteps. No second Hive beast; the Deepmaw stays their one war beast.

Flight per race, decided: Orcs get a fuel-burst rocket pack: hold jump to thrust up or forward, burns fuel fast, loud, short and strong; for jumping walls and diving into fights, not long trips. Angels get true free flight in daylight under open sky; at night or underground the wings only glide like an elytra. Elves cast flight as a spell (levitate and a wind leap) paid with Iron's Spells mana, with a fallback cost when Iron's Spells isn't installed.

Twilight Forest is out (CurseForge-only). In its place the pack runs The Aether and Deeper and Darker, both crossed over with Warfront as optional integrations: the Aether is the angels' homeland and the Otherside (Deeper and Darker's dimension) the Hive's; Fallen Host raids come down from the Aether and Swarm raids rise from the Otherside; their ores and sculk materials fuel mana and build altars; angel wings and the angels' war beast (an armored Moa) come from the Aether, Hive gear or a beast from the Otherside; faction outposts and raid chests also appear in both dimensions as late-game raids.

Towers get real 3D models before any new tower types: the Arrow Tower, Arcane Spire and Healing Shrine each get a proper model, styled by the race of the player who placed it. New tower types come later.

Enemy factions keep their race's body and colors, plus one signature trim piece each so you can read them at a glance: Marauder Horde (orc): war paint stripes and bone trophies on the belt and shoulders; Black Legion (human): a black tabard with a white skull and a spiked pauldron; Burning Horde (demon): smoldering chains and a soot-blackened brand on the chest; The Swarm (Hive): glowing acid sacs on the back and jagged black chitin spurs; Silverwood Reavers (elf): thorn-vine wraps and a pale antler-bone mask; Ironbeard Clan (dwarf): a rune-etched iron face guard and braided beard rings; Fallen Host (angel): torn, ash-gray wings and a cracked, dimmed halo.

The full-size demons (Hellguard, Fiend, Archfiend, Hellknight) are armored hellknights: faceless black-iron plate, horns breaking through the helm, hooves, and ember-orange fire glowing through the visor and plate seams, so they never read as Black Legion humans. The Blood Witch wears blood-red robes over light black-iron plate with a horned hood. Imps stay the small winged caste.
Sizes follow rank: soldiers stay at their race's size, Captains are 15% bigger and Champions 30% bigger (the Hive Ravager keeps its 35%), so heroes stand out on the field. Role doesn't change size.

Siege outposts: every 5th wave raises a temporary enemy outpost near the War Standard, and the siege can't be won while it stands. It scales with the wave: a watchtower camp early, a small walled fort later. Until it is taken it keeps sending raiders, so you have to go on the attack. At its heart sits a big raid chest, a different one for each enemy faction (bone chest for demons, chitin pod for the Swarm and so on). Loot it, break it, and the whole outpost despawns.

Units are mortal. Rank-and-file troops and workers die for good and are re-summoned with mana. Captains, Champions and war beasts fall instead of dying: revive them on the field within about 60 seconds, or they return to the altar after a cooldown for part of their mana cost.

No separate guard unit: any battle unit can be put on guard duty (holds a spot, short beat) or patrol duty (ranges about 16 blocks) and raises the alarm. Sneak + right-click it to cycle guard, patrol and back to the army.
The orc non-combat roles (farmer and builder) are goblins.

Humans fly with the Mana Glider: worn in the chest slot and launched like an elytra, human only. It glides rather than dives, and a Mana Shard used mid-flight gives a burst of speed. Repaired with Mana Crystals.

Demon dark magic is Soul Harvest: every kill takes a soul (up to 10), healing 2 health and adding 2% attack damage per soul. With 10 souls the next hit unleashes a Soul Burst: +6 damage to the target and 4 to enemies within 3 blocks, spending every soul. Souls are lost on death. Works for demon players and soldiers.

Orcs build Rage by landing and taking hits (10 and 15 points); at 100 they go into a Frenzy for 8 seconds: +30% damage, +20% attack speed, +15% speed, but 15% more damage taken. Frenzied orc soldiers don't rout. Rage drains after 3 seconds out of combat. Works for orc players and soldiers.

Elves are master archers: their arrows fly 20% faster and hit 25% harder, and a shot from 16+ blocks hits a further 25% harder and makes the target glow for 5 seconds. Elf soldier archers keep their tighter aim. Works for elf players and soldiers.

Each race casts one Iron's Spells school 25% stronger and one 10% weaker: Human Evocation (weak Eldritch), Elf Nature (weak Fire), Dwarf Lightning (weak Ender), Orc Blood (weak Evocation), Demon Fire (weak Holy), Angel Holy (weak Blood), Hive Eldritch (weak Holy). It works through Iron's spell power attributes, so Warfront runs fine without Iron's Spells.
Captains need a level 2 base and Champions a level 4 base before an altar will summon them. Everyone else needs only a complete altar and the mana.

Base level needs two things at once: buildings on the base's mana network (wells, pylons, towers, altars) and siege waves won at a War Standard on that network. The lower of the two sets the level, so it can't be built or fought up alone. Levels 2 to 5 need 6/12/20/30 buildings and 3/8/15/25 waves. Each level allows 2 war beasts (10 at level 5). If the War Standard falls, its wave count is lost.
The Lancer-Drone is approved: a sturdy, armored four-armed ant warrior gripping a plain spear in both upper hands, rear of the haft clear of the legs, short-fingered lower hands, no throwing blade.
Sculk-dark colors; stronger underground and weaker in sunlight; Swarm raids tunnel up near their target; new Hive players start in a cave.

The Deepmaw is a lobster centaur: the lobster carapace, eight legs and tail, with an upright human-like torso and claws held out to the sides, in the Hive's sculk look, with thick claw arms and the reference's crowned face. Approved.
Beasts are rare altar units: 2 per base level, up to 10 per commander at base level 5.
Keep Warfront compatible with other mods: vanilla attributes, effects, tags and capabilities; optional integrations only.
The Hive spearman (Lancer-Drone) follows your reference: a four-armed ant-warrior with a double-bladed polearm.
The Hive gets a large burrowing beast unit based on your reference (hive-beast.png). It's a unit, not the player character.
The Demons get a large beast unit: a bone-white, skeletal flier with red barbs, insect-like wings and a scorpion stinger tail, from your reference.
Fantastical creatures come later: a few assigned to each race, most of them neutral.

Most player races get their own player model and some form of flight. Orcs: a jetpack or similar tech, not wings. Angels: angel wings. Elves: flight magic. Humans: the Mana Glider. Demons already fly on their wings. Dwarves tunnel instead of flying. Flight mechanics are decided (see the flight decision); the player models wait on your references.
The Hive becomes a Warden and sculk-like underground race that builds its keeps in caves. Redesign comes after the mana system.
Imps are one demon species. They only fill the Impaler and Firecaster roles.
Builders, farmers and guards look plain and humanoid in every race.
Mana is base power: wells store it, pylons extend range, towers and the altar draw from it. No personal mana bar.
Manabloom grows shards (everyday fuel); mana ore gives crystals (dense fuel and building material).
Units are summoned at a multiblock altar with a menu.
Oryx-style head, bare hands and feet, wings that fold at the elbow, flight without an elytra.
